verses.1: And there was a man named Bila’el. His name was Seba, son of Cairi. He was my right-hand man. He said, “We have no share in David’s inheritance. We will not receive any portion from the son of Jesse. Israel will be our dwelling place.”
verses.2: And every man of Israel rose up against David, against Sheba’s son Rehoboam. And all the Jews from the land of Judah gathered together to oppose their king, from the Jordan River all the way to Jerusalem.
verses.3: David went to Jerusalem and took the king’s ten women, who were responsible for taking care of the palace. He gave them rooms to live in. But they never came to live there. They remained in a state of misery until today.
verses.4: And the king said to Amasa, “I am crying out for help from the people of Judah. They have been in distress for three days, and you are standing here.”
verses.5: And Amasai went to call the Jews. He chose one from among those who were appointed as leaders.
verses.6: And David said to Abishai, “Now, seven sons of Reuben from Abshalom have become our enemies. You must take your servants and chase after them. Otherwise, they will find cities in ruins, and we will be saved.”
verses.7: And after them went the people of Joab, and Keret, and Phelat. All the tribes also went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba’s son, Bichri.
verses.8: They stood before that huge stone, which was placed in the middle of the field. Yavuah was bound with ropes, and on his head there were ropes also. These ropes were tied around his wrists. Then he was taken away.
verses.9: And Yoav said to Amasa, “You are my brother. Let me take your right hand in my own.” Yoav did so when Amasa was old enough to be kissed.
verses.10: And Amashah was not preserved in the furnace that was in Yoav’s hands. He was thrown into the furnace, and his body was turned to dust. He died. Yoav and Abishai, his brothers, pursued Seba, the son of Bukki.
verses.11: And a man stood up from the men of Joab’s army, and said, “Who is it who desires Joab, and who is it who loves David more than Joab?”
verses.12: And Amashah was lying in the blood within the pit. The man saw that all the people had stood around him. He then pulled Amashah out of the pit and threw a garment over him, just as everyone else who came to see him did.
verses.13: As he stepped out of the tent, every man followed after Yoav, in order to follow after Sheba’s son.
verses.14: And it spread throughout all the tribes of Israel, including Bethel and Bechai, as well as all the cities. They gathered together and came forward.
verses.15: And they came and set up a funeral pile for him in the city. They poured blood into it, and all the people who were involved in his murder stood there, ready to throw stones at him.
verses.16: And a wise woman from the city called out to Yoav, “Come here quickly!” She said, “I want to speak with you.”
verses.17: And he came to her. She said, “You are Yoav.” He replied, “I am.” She said to him, “Listen to your words of truth.” He replied, “I will listen.”
verses.18: And it was said, “Let them speak in the past. Let them say that Sheol will question them in sorrow.” And so it happened.
verses.19: I am the Son of Israel’s promise. You want to destroy a city and its people in Israel. Why do you want to destroy the land of Jehovah?
verses.20: And Joab said, “Alas, alas for me! What will happen if I burn it down and destroy it?”
verses.21: It is not true that anyone from the land of Efraim, whose name was Ben-Bikri, took hold of King David and handed him over to his own hands. Then she left the city. The woman said to Yoav, “Look! His head has been taken away from us.”
verses.22: And the woman went before all the people with her wisdom. They chose seven sons from among them, and they sent them to Joab. Joab put them in prison. Then each man returned to his own house. Joab went back to Jerusalem and reported to the king.
verses.23: And Joshua went before all the Israelites and their children. Yehoyada knew about my fate and my punishment.
verses.24: And Adram will rule over the people, and Yehoshafat will be the judge of Ahilud’s descendants.
verses.25: And Shuva was a scribe, and Zadok and Ebiatar were priests.
verses.26: And also Eriya the Yari was a priest to David.
